messages.subject: Derivative of user-supplied function
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

In some models, it is helpful for the user to supply a function, and then have a calculation in the function evaluating the joint distribution of fixed and random effects that depends on the gradient of that function.  It is of course possible to calculate the gradient externally and supply that, but it would be easier (and perhaps less prone to transcription errors) to have TMB do the gradient calculation internally.  This arises, e.g., in a movement model when advection is driven by the gradient of a user-supplied and parametric preference function, where we supply  and want to calculate , where  and  might be functions of random effects, and hence we need higher-order gradients available for .

Is there any simple example or high-level function to do this?

I see some related concepts in:
the examples for defining atomics in TINY_AD <https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/adaptive_integration_8cpp-example.html>
the Laplace example <https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/laplace_8cpp-example.html> and related discussions <https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/229>, although I'm not sure if there's any easier way to do that now using the framework = "TMBad"
Basically, I'm wondering if there's some method or example that's a little easier to understand.

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Derivative of user-supplied function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jim, There are a couple of pretty simple examples of usage of gradients and hessians in the wham package to internally calculate FMSY and F at X%SPR here <https://github.com/timjmiller/wham/blob/6c30301d5b68c2bb0c0330cc4f112432c7950dfd/src/helper_functions.hpp#L443>. There may be better ways to do that though.

Thanks for asking this though because it reminded me that I have a related question:

Does anyone know if there is an issue with using "expm" (matrix exponential) in functions like this? I have one like those referenced above, but it causes my TMB function to hang indefinitely (without crashing) when output from that is ADREPORTed.

I see here <https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/b380fe8e78d16aba38d755ad4efbea3139d92212/TMB/inst/include/expm.hpp#L188> something about expm being available for derivative orders 0-3, but perhaps using it in these functions of hessians and gradients requires more derivatives available? If so, how might I obtain the necessary higher order derivatives?

Thanks,
Tim

messages.body_plain:
About expm: It appears, from the source you link to, that if evaluated for orders higher than 3 you get the error  "expm: order not implemented.". So, something else must be the problem. Note that expm derivatives are evaluated for every quantity you ADREPORT, which might explain the long running time.
